links.outcome: Whether predefined drift and performance thresholds trigger alarms and deployment decisions in simulated iterations
links.effect: Across 11 simulated sepsis iterations: 8 APPROVE, 1 CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, 1 CLINICAL REVIEW, 1 REJECT; ALARM signals co-issued at iterations 8 and 10; drift detected before observable performance degradation.
links.quote: AEGIS detected drift before observable performance degradation.

unlisted_practices: Four-category deployment decision taxonomy (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, CLINICAL REVIEW, REJECT) with independent post-market surveillance ALARM signal for detecting when no deployable model exists

screen.reason: Evaluates an operational governance and post-market surveillance framework (AEGIS) for adaptive medical AI across simulated continuous learning iterations in sepsis prediction and brain tumor segmentation.

primary.practice: post-market surveillance and change-control governance infrastructure
